newsitem.title: USA: Cominco says would invest more in Anvil.
newsitem.headline: Cominco says would invest more in Anvil.

text.p: Cominco Ltd said it would be prepared to plough more cash into Anvil Range Mining Corp in order to help restart the latter's Faro mine, but there was still no intention to take a controlling stake in the troubled company, Cominco's president and CEO David Thompson said.

"We are not interested in taking control," Thompson said during a presentation at the American Zinc Association conference here. "We think the mine (Faro) has the possibility to make good earnings but at obviously higher (zinc) prices."
Cominco is proposing to buy 4.1 million shares in Anvil Range for C$2.30 per share to become a 28 percent shareholder in the company.
Anvil was forced to shut down its Faro zinc and lead mine in December because it had too little cash and metal prices were hurting.
"We would put in some more money," Thompson told Reuters. "But we don't see ourselves being the only provider of money."
Anvil has said the cash injection from Cominco alone would not be enough to restart Faro which was shuttered in December.
Another company, Mineral Resources Corp, has also indicated it would like to take control of Anvil Range.
But Thompson said that Anvil's other major shareholder, Hyundai of Korea "is with us. They welcome our investment."
After Cominco's share acquisition at Anvil, Hyundai's stake will be diluted from some 25 percent, to 20 percent, Thompson said. Combined Hyundai and Cominco would hold 48 percent.

Miners and smelters are gathered here amid negotiations to settle this year's zinc and lead concentrates sales. Several smelter officials have said that uncertainty hanging over when Faro will be restarted is having an effect on the treatment charge talks, along with MIM Holding's cutback in mined output.
